description: Multi-block Δτ_M probe (NOT a c_3 derivation). Combines the exact pre-archimedean per-block closed forms χ_λ(Δ_T_β)(q) — (3) and (1,1,1) from qbeta-per-block-paper-closed-forms.witness.json, (2,1) in the CANONICAL borromean intra-nucleon ordering since 2026-09-07 (beans qou-hu1f / qou-eddc) — with a NON-CANONICAL rational surrogate for the Wenzl y_λ(q) weights (canonical y_λ involves √q) to emit Δτ_M(q) as a rational function of q. Reports: (1) the closed form, (2) its Taylor expansion around q=1 in w=q−1 to 12 orders, (3) the cross-anchor swing of Δτ_M between q_proton and q_muon (the NEAR-MATCH diagnostic for the Δτ_M object — NOT for c_3, which requires the open f-map). c_3 is explicitly recorded as NOT_DERIVED. NO FITS.

grouped_frame_superseded.note: All-σ₀-then-all-σ₁ intra-nucleon word, canonical until the qou-hu1f ruling of 2026-09-05. Only the 2-dimensional (2,1) block differs; (3) and (1,1,1) are 1-dimensional, so their generators commute and the ordering cannot reach them. The two frames agree at orders 0-2 (asserted above) and diverge from order 3.

data.c_3_status: NEAR-MATCH (open). The Δτ_M closed form computed here does NOT yield c_3 directly. The f-map transform between Δτ_M's w = q-1 expansion and the Q_β ladder's u = b·ℏ_q² expansion is the missing keystone (open). Per the 1ppQ-Q_β ledger, c_3 = -2 remains a NEAR-MATCH (flip-flop history #1-5) — NOT wired as Taylor-exact. data.structural_note: Δτ_M(q) is a rational function of q (no √ — symbolic in q²). The symmetric (3) ↔ (1,1,1) ↔ q ↔ 1/q pairing under antipode is exact at the rational-function level. NOTE (2026-09-07): the earlier claim here that (2,1) is 'linear in h' described the grouped frame, where χ_(2,1) = −h³/4 − h/2; in the canonical borromean frame it is h⁹/2 + 11h⁷/4 + 17h⁵/4 + 5h³/4 − h/2. Both are odd in h — bar-parity survives the reordering — and both have the same −h/2 leading term, which is why the classical point and the (q²−1) factor are frame-independent. The cross-anchor swing IS the order-of-magnitude diagnostic for whether c_3 derives from this object exactly or is a near-match.
